content_list.content_text: The production of political and psychological thrillers in 1970s Hollywood is generally interpreted as a paranoid reaction to the Watergate scandal and a residue of the witch hunt against communists in the 1950s. Other contributing factors include the specter of the Vietnam War and the feeling among liberals that, although everyone hated the war, it went on because of the government's stubbornness.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from All the President's Men
information.contentText: Unlike the book, the film covers only the first seven months of the Watergate scandal, from the break-in to Nixon's second inauguration on January 20, 1973. The film introduced the catchphrase "follow the money" in relation to the case, which did not appear in the book or in any Watergate documentation.

content_list.content_text: There was a growing sense that Hollywood did not understand its audience. All of this combined left the film world insecure and the nation introspective. The prototype of Hollywood conspiracy films is The Manchurian Candidate (1962), directed by John Frankenheimer (1920-2002). While seemingly about a communist plot against the American government, the film reveals that the conspiracy is the work of homegrown politicians and military leaders. During the 1960s and 1970s, films portraying the authorities as ambiguous and corrupt became common.

However, Hollywood's paranoia peaked with the Watergate scandal in 1972. A definite sense of unease became visible in many Hollywood genres: in Westerns such as Pat Garrett & Billy the Kid (1973), political dramas such as The Candidate (1972), gangster films such as The Godfather Part II (1974), and science fiction works such as Soylent Green (1973). In each of them, the forces of American power and politics are portrayed as untrustworthy, exploiting ordinary people for personal or corporate gain.

information.contentText: The plot revolves around a surveillance expert and the moral dilemma he faces when his recordings reveal a possible murder. Coppola cited the 1966 film Blow-Up as an influence. However, because the film was released in theaters just a few months before Richard Nixon resigned the presidency, he felt that audiences interpreted the film as a reaction to the Watergate scandal.

content_list.content_text: Soylent Green presents the darkest vision, portraying the New York of 2017 as a dystopia in which people unwittingly live as cannibals and corrupt officials help cover up the truth. The iconic film of the period is The Parallax View (1974), a dark thriller directed by Alan J. Pakula (1928-1998) in which the hippie reporter played by Warren Beatty (b. 1937) investigates the Kennedy-style assassination of a committed American senator and stumbles upon a plot that reaches the highest echelons of business and government.

quote.quote: Coppola's cerebral classic of paranoia and surveillance remains superb and is even more relevant in the age of CCTV and security.
quote.author: Peter Bradshaw on The Conversation (1974)

content_list.content_text: The film set the stylistic template for the conspiracy film: labyrinthine narrative, booming sound effects, overlapping dialogue, brutal steel-and-glass architecture, and sparing use of music on the soundtrack. The Conversation (1974), directed by Francis Ford Coppola (b. 1939), and Night Moves (1975), by Arthur Penn (1922-2010), adopt an equally cold, modernist style but tell more intimate stories. Both films star Gene Hackman as a private investigator who confronts forces far beyond his control and loses his identity in the process.

information.contentText: The screenplay was based on Harry Harrison's novel Make Room! Make Room! (1966), which is set in the year 1999 and deals with overpopulation and the overuse of resources, leading to rising poverty, food shortages, and social disorder. Harrison was contractually denied control over the screenplay and was not told during negotiations that Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer was buying the film rights.

content_list.content_text: In these films, the doomed hero, though intelligent and committed, becomes a victim not only of powerful outside influences but also of his own emotional weakness, his instability, and his obsessive nature.

The only film to deal directly with the Watergate scandal was All the President's Men (1976). Despite its narrative complexity and fact-packed screenplay, the film was a hit with an audience desperate to leave the Nixon era behind. After it, with Nixon defeated and the Vietnam War over, paranoia began to give way to the optimism of films such as Star Wars (1977). Traces remained in works such as Marathon Man (1976), directed by John Schlesinger (1926-2003), although the corrupting force in that film belongs not to a rotten government organization but to an individual, in the form of a Nazi war criminal.

movies.title: All the President's Men
movies.overview: In the run-up to the 1972 elections, Washington Post reporter Bob Woodward covers what seems to be a minor break-in at the Democratic Party National Headquarters. He is surprised to find top lawyers already on the defense case, and the discovery of names and addresses of Republican fund organizers on the accused further arouses his suspicions. After the editor of the Post runs with the story and assigns Woodward and Carl Bernstein to it, they find the trail leading higher and higher in the Republican Party—and eventually into the White House itself.

movies.title: The Conversation
movies.overview: Surveillance expert Harry Caul is hired by a mysterious client's brusque aide to tail a young couple. Tracking the pair through San Francisco's Union Square, Caul and his associate Stan manage to record a cryptic conversation between them. Tormented by memories of a previous case that ended badly, Caul becomes obsessed with the resulting tape, trying to determine if the couple are in danger.

movies.title: Soylent Green
movies.overview: In an overpopulated futuristic Earth, a New York police detective finds himself marked for murder by government agents when he gets too close to a bizarre state secret involving the origins of a revolutionary and needed new foodstuff.

movies.title: The Parallax View
movies.overview: An ambitious reporter, investigating a senator's assassination, realizes witnesses to the shooting are systematically dying and discovers a multi-million dollar corporation which serves as a front for the recruitment of political assassins.

movies.title: Marathon Man
movies.overview: A graduate student and obsessive runner in New York is drawn into a mysterious plot involving his brother, a member of the secretive Division.

movies.title: The Anderson Tapes
movies.overview: Thief Duke Anderson—just released from ten years in jail—takes up with his old girlfriend in her posh apartment block, and makes plans to rob the entire building. What he doesn't know is that his every move is being recorded on audio and video, although he is not the subject of any surveillance.

movies.title: Klute
movies.overview: A high-priced call girl is forced to depend on a reluctant private eye when she is stalked by a psychopath.

movies.title: Night Moves
movies.overview: Private detective and former football player Harry Moseby gets hired on to what seems a standard missing person case, as a former Hollywood actress whose only major roles came thanks to being married to a studio mogul wants Moseby to find and return her daughter. Harry travels to Florida to find her, but he begins to see a connection between the runaway girl, the world of Hollywood stuntmen, and a suspicious mechanic when an unsolved murder comes to light.

movies.title: Nashville
movies.overview: The intersecting stories of twenty-four characters—from country star to wannabe to reporter to waitress— connect to the music business in Nashville, Tennessee.

movies.title: Coma
movies.overview: A young woman doctor discovers something sinister going on in her hospital. Relatively healthy patients are having 'complications' during simple operations and ending up in comas. The patients are then shipped off to an institute that looks after them. The young doctor suspects there is more to this than meets the eye.

movies.title: Capricorn One
movies.overview: In order to protect the reputation of the American space program, a team of scientists stages a phony Mars landing. Willingly participating in the deception are a trio of well-meaning astronauts, who become liabilities when their space capsule is reported lost on re-entry. Now, with the help of a crusading reporter, they must battle a sinister conspiracy that will stop at nothing to keep the truth.

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 1970 to 1989
content_list.description: The Exorcist is released, making audiences around the world sick and causing them to faint, creating a global hysteria. The first blockbuster is released: Jaws; meanwhile, auteur cinema grows with Martin Scorsese and other great directors. The '80s arrive with low-budget productions and era-defining comedies.
